## [AWS News Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/)

# How to Use the New AWS Application Migration Service for Lift-and-Shift Migrations

|  |
| --- |
| [Voiced by Polly](https://aws.amazon.com/polly/) |

![Voiced by Polly](https://a0.awsstatic.com/aws-blog/images/Voiced_by_Amazon_Polly_EN.png)

Since AWS acquired CloudEndure in 2019, our new colleagues have offered CloudEndure Migration and CloudEndure Disaster Recovery. CloudEndure Migration can move applications from any physical, virtual, or cloud-based infrastructure to AWS at no charge. This complements AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS), which is an agentless service for migrating on-premises workloads to AWS. CloudEndure Disaster Recovery is a separate business continuity offering, designed to help you minimize downtime and data loss. It continuously replicates the contents of your on-premises, virtual, or cloud-based systems to a low-cost staging area in the AWS Region of your choice, within the confines of your AWS account. This offer is available to all AWS customers and partners.

Recently, we launched [AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN)](https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/) (AWS MGN), which we now recommend as the primary migration service for lift-and-shift migrations to AWS. We encourage customers who are currently using CloudEndure Migration or AWS SMS to switch to AWS MGN for future migrations. AWS MGN enables organizations to move applications to AWS without having to make any changes to the applications, their architecture, or the migrated servers.

With AWS MGN, you can minimize time-intensive, error-prone manual processes by automatically replicating entire servers and converting your source servers from physical, virtual, or cloud infrastructure to run natively on AWS. The service simplifies your migration by enabling you to use the same automated process for a wide range of applications. By launching non-disruptive tests before migrating, you can be confident that your most critical applications such as SAP, Oracle, and SQL Server will work seamlessly on AWS.

AWS MGN reduces overall migration costs because there is no need to invest in multiple migration solutions, specialized cloud development, or application-specific skills. This is because AWS MGN can be used to migrate any application from any source infrastructure that runs supported operating systems.

**How AWS MGN Works**
  
To migrate to AWS, you install the AWS MGN Replication Agent on your source servers and then view and define replication settings in the AWS MGN console. AWS MGN uses these settings to create and manage a staging area subnet with lightweight [Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/) instances, that act as replication servers used to replicate data between your source servers and AWS.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/15/2021-aws-mgn-how-it-works.jpg)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/15/2021-aws-mgn-how-it-works.jpg)

Replication servers receive data from the agent running on your source servers and write this data to the [Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)](https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/) volumes. Your replicated data is compressed and encrypted in transit and at rest using EBS encryption. AWS MGN keeps your source servers up to date on AWS using continuous, block-level data replication. It uses your defined launch settings to launch instances when you conduct non-disruptive tests or perform a cutover.

When you launch test or cutover instances, AWS MGN converts your source servers to boot and run natively on AWS. After confirming that your launched instances are operating properly on AWS, you can decommission your source servers. You can then choose to modernize your applications by using AWS services and capabilities.

**AWS MGN – Getting Started** To get started, create the replication settings template in the AWS MGN[console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/mgn/home). This template will determine how data replication will work for each newly added source server. Before you configure your template, ensure that you meet the [network requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/preparing-environments.html) for running AWS MGN.

In the AWS MGN console, choose **Get started** to create the template.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-getting-started.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-getting-started.png)

The replication settings configured in this template will be applied to each newly added source server. You can change the settings at any time for any individual source server or group of source servers.

Replication servers are lightweight EC2 instances that are used to replicate data between your source servers and AWS. They are automatically launched and terminated as needed. You can use data routing and throttling settings to control how data is routed from your source servers to the replication servers.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-replication-template.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-replication-template.png)

After you create your template, you can add your source servers. To edit your template, in the left navigation pane, choose **Settings**. You can edit individual server replication settings after you add your source servers.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-firstsourceservers.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-firstsourceservers.png)

To add source servers to AWS MGN, install the AWS MGN Replication Agent on them. You can install the agent on servers running Linux and Windows. For more information, see [adding source servers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/adding-servers.html) in the documentation.

For example, download the `aws-replication-installer-init.py` agent installer with the `wget` command and run the installation script in your Linux source server.

`aws-replication-installer-init.py`
`wget`

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-servers-linuxagent.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-servers-linuxagent.png)

After the AWS Replication Agent is installed, the server will be added to AWS MGN console and undergo the initial sync process.​

The **Source Servers** page displays a list of source servers. Each row in the list represents a single server. The [migration lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/lifecycle.html) column shows the current state of each source server. After the initial sync process has been completed successfully, data replication will start automatically.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-server-1.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-server-1.png)

After you have added your source servers, you must configure the launch settings for each server. The launch settings are a set of instructions that determine how a test or cutover instance will be launched for each source server on AWS.

You must configure the launch settings before you launch test or cutover instances. To access the launch settings, choose the host name of a source server and then navigate to the **Launch settings** tab.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-launch-settings.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-launch-settings.png)

After you have added your source servers and configured their launch settings, you are ready to launch a test instance. You must test the migration of your source servers to AWS before you initiate a cutover, to verify that your source servers function properly in the AWS environment.

To launch a test or cutover instance for a single source server or multiple source servers, on the **Source Servers** page, select the checkbox for each server for which you want to launch a test instance.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-test-cutover-servers-1.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/22/2021-aws-mgn-source-test-cutover-servers-1.png)

You can test one source server at a time or multiple source servers simultaneously. For each source server, you will be informed of the success or failure of the test. Choose **Launch test instances** to start the test, and then choose **Launch**.

When the test has started, the console will display a **Launch job started** message. To view the specific job for the test launch, choose **View job details**.

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-finish-test-jobs.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-finish-test-jobs.png)

Use the **Migration dashboard** tab to monitor the progress in relation to the [migration lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/lifecycle.html).

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-migration-dashboard.png)

![](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2021/04/14/2021-aws-mgn-migration-dashboard.png)

As a best practice, perform a test at least one week before you plan to migrate your source servers. This allows you time to identify and solve problems before the cutover takes place. After you launch the test instances, use SSH (Linux) or RDP (Windows) to connect to your instance and ensure that everything is working correctly.

After you have finalized the testing of your source servers, you are ready for a cutover. It’s a best practice to schedule the cutover time in advance. After the cutover action is performed, the server is considered migrated, and you should redirect your users from your original source servers to the migrated ones.

If you are completely done with your migration and performed a successful cutover, you can finalize the cutover. This will change your source servers’ migration lifecycle status to **Cutover complete**, indicating that the cutover is complete and that the migration has been performed successfully.

**Monitoring and Troubleshooting**
  
You can monitor AWS MGN using [Amazon CloudWatch](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/), [Amazon EventBridge](https://aws.amazon.com/eventbridge), and AWS CloudTrail, which collect raw data and process it into readable, near-real-time metrics. For more information, see [Monitoring Application Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/monitoring-overview.html) in the documentation.

If you encounter any issues and want to launch new test or cutover instances, you can revert the test or cutover action. This will revert your source servers lifecycle status to the previous stage, indicating that these servers have not undergone cutover. During a revert, you will also have the option to delete your test or cutover instances for cost-saving purposes. For more information, see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/troubleshooting.html) in the documentation.

**Now Available** [AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN)](https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/) (AWS MGN) is now available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), US East (Ohio), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Europe (Ireland), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (Stockholm). If your preferred AWS Region is not currently supported by AWS MGN, consider using [CloudEndure Migration](https://console.cloudendure.com/#/register/register). If you cannot install an agent on your servers, consider using [AWS Server Migration Service](https://aws.amazon.com/server-migration-service/) (AWS SMS).

Although the use of AWS MGN is free for 90 days, you will incur charges for any AWS infrastructure that is provisioned during migration and after cutover. For more information, see the AWS MGN[pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/pricing/).

args.summary:
This AWS News Blog article announces and provides a comprehensive guide to using the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN), which AWS recommends as the primary migration service for lift-and-shift migrations to AWS. The service is the evolution of CloudEndure Migration (which AWS acquired in 2019) and complements AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS), with AWS encouraging customers using CloudEndure Migration or AWS SMS to switch to AWS MGN.

Key features of AWS MGN include: automatic replication of entire servers from physical, virtual, or cloud infrastructure to run natively on AWS without application changes; support for critical applications like SAP, Oracle, and SQL Server; and reduced migration costs by eliminating the need for multiple migration solutions or specialized skills. The service is free to use for 90 days, with charges applying only for provisioned AWS infrastructure during and after migration.

The migration process involves: (1) installing the AWS MGN Replication Agent on source servers (Linux and Windows supported), (2) creating a replication settings template in the AWS MGN console, (3) configuring launch settings for each source server, (4) running non-disruptive test launches (best practice: at least one week before planned migration), and (5) performing cutover and finalizing to complete the migration. Replication works via lightweight EC2 instances that compress and encrypt data (using EBS encryption) during continuous, block-level replication to staging areas.

The service is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), US East (Ohio), Asia Pacific (Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore), and Europe (Ireland, Frankfurt, Stockholm). Monitoring is supported via Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS CloudTrail. For unsupported regions, AWS suggests CloudEndure Migration; for environments where agents cannot be installed, AWS SMS remains an option. The article was written by Channy Yun, Lead Blogger of AWS News Blog and Principal Developer Advocate for AWS Cloud.
args.key_excerpts: "AWS MGN enables organizations to move applications to AWS without having to make any changes to the applications, their architecture, or the migrated servers."

This is the AWS Transform MGN (Application Migration Service) resources page, which serves as a central hub for documentation, training, tutorials, case studies, and architecture resources for AWS's server migration service. The page positions AWS as "the world's most comprehensive cloud, enabling organizations to accelerate innovation, reduce costs, and scale more efficiently."

Key resource categories include:
- **Documentation & Training**: Technical documentation with a Getting Started Guide, free online technical training, access to the AWS Transform MGN Console for replication, and APN Partner materials for partners helping customers with lift-and-shift migrations.
- **Tutorials & Demos**: Video tutorials covering MGN Connector (automating replication agent installation), data replication, managing migrations, and re:Invent presentations, plus additional demos on modernization, architecture, and launch templates.
- **Architecture Diagrams**: Five downloadable PDFs covering standard and modernization options for general architecture and network architecture, including a no-internet-access network configuration.
- **Case Studies**: Featured customer stories include 3M (migrating thousands of applications), Mayden (migrating 300 servers in 6 weeks), SmartSearch, Veolia (34 business-critical applications), University of West Indies Open Campus (50% TCO savings), Bosa Development, Finnair, World Fuel Services (20 data centers in 2 years, 50% cost reduction), and Arista Group (20% lower IT costs).
- **Additional Resources**: AWS Summit DC 2022 session on compliance and security, online tech talks, a step-by-step migration workshop, and eBooks on cloud migration ("Move and Improve" and "Getting Started with Cloud Migration").
- **Next Steps**: AWS Migration Acceleration Program for large-scale migrations, AWS Free Tier signup, and getting started in the AWS Application Migration Service console.

The page targets organizations seeking to migrate and modernize applications to AWS using the Application Migration Service (formerly known as AWS Application Migration Service / MGN).

# AWS Application Migration Service: Process, Pricing, and Best Practices

* Faddom

Read Time:   6 minutes

## What Is AWS Application Migration Service?

AWS [Application Migration](https://faddom.com/what-is-application-migration/) Service (AWS MGN) is a tool designed to simplify the process of migrating applications to AWS. It automates tasks required for moving applications from on-premises or other cloud environments to AWS, ensuring minimal downtime and maintaining data integrity.

The service supports a range of source environments, including physical servers, virtual machines, and other clouds. It can replicate servers in real-time, allowing organizations to keep their applications running while migration takes place. This replication process is optimized for compatibility with AWS, ensuring that applications can run in the new environment with little to no modification needed.

## Use Cases of AWS Application Migration Service

AWS Application Migration Service supports various scenarios:

* **Data Center Migration:** Organizations can move their entire data center workloads to AWS with minimal downtime. These include enterprise applications such as SAP, Oracle, and SQL Server that run on physical servers or virtualized environments like VMware vSphere and Microsoft Hyper-V. The continuous replication feature ensures that applications remain up-to-date and operational during the migration process.
* **Disaster Recovery:** AWS MGN can be used to set up a disaster recovery environment in AWS. By continuously replicating on-premises data to the cloud, businesses can quickly failover to AWS in the event of a disaster, ensuring business continuity.
* **Test and Development:** Organizations can replicate production environments to AWS to create isolated test and development environments. This allows for safe testing and development without impacting the production systems.
* **Cloud-to-Cloud Migration:** AWS MGN supports migration from other cloud environments to AWS. This flexibility helps organizations consolidate their cloud infrastructure within AWS. MGN also supports moving workloads across different AWS Regions, Availability Zones, or accounts.
* **Physical to Cloud Migration:** For businesses with physical servers, AWS MGN facilitates the migration to the cloud without the need for significant modifications to the applications, simplifying the transition process. The service minimizes downtime and ensures a smooth transition to the cloud.

## AWS Application Migration Service Pricing

**Free use for 90 days**

AWS Application Migration Service allows users to start their migration projects with minimal initial costs. Each source server eligible for migration can use MGN for free for up to 2,160 hours, which equates to 90 days of continuous use.

The free period starts as soon as the AWS Replication Agent is installed on the source server and continues throughout the active replication phase.

**Costs beyond the free period**

If the migration of a server extends beyond the free period, AWS charges $0.042 per hour for continued replication, amounting to approximately $30 per server per month.

**Additional charges**

During both the free and paid phases, users will incur additional charges for AWS infrastructure used to support data replication. These costs include resources such as Amazon EC2 for compute power and Amazon EBS for storage, which are provisioned when launching test or cutover instances.

## Tips from the Expert

In my experience, here are tips that can help you better utilize AWS Application Migration Service:

1. **Use Infrastructure as Code (IaC)**

   After migration, automate your infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation or Terraform. This ensures consistent setups, simplifies scaling, and aids in disaster recovery planning.
2. **Minimize storage costs**

   Exclude non-critical data during replication and manage snapshots with AWS Data Lifecycle Manager to reduce ongoing storage expenses without compromising essential data.
3. **Pre-warm instances for smooth cutover**

   Launch test instances with the same configuration as your production servers ahead of the cutover. This ensures faster transitions and minimizes downtime during the migration window.
4. **Monitor replication health with CloudWatch**

   Set up AWS CloudWatch to monitor replication metrics and establish alarms for issues like latency or failed replication. Proactive monitoring avoids delays and ensures a smooth migration process.
5. **Prepare a rollback strategy**

   Before the cutover, take a full backup snapshot of your source servers. This provides a fallback option to quickly revert to the original environment if unexpected issues occur.

## The AWS Application Migration Service Workflow

The AWS MGN workflow involves these stages:

1. The organization installs the AWS Replication Agent on the source server. For environments using vCenter, an agentless replication feature is available, requiring the installation of the AWS MGN vCenter Client instead.
2. The service performs an initial synchronization of the source server to AWS, ensuring that a consistent copy of the application data is available in the cloud.
3. Once the initial sync is complete, test instances are launched in AWS to verify application functionality in the new environment. This testing phase involves performing acceptance tests on these instances.
4. If testing succeeds without issues, these test instances are then finalized and deleted.
5. The next step involves waiting for a designated cutover window, at which point traffic is redirected to the new environment in AWS.
6. Once the applications are up and running in AWS, the organization can stop its operational services on the source server.
7. The final step is launching a cutover instance in AWS. The organization confirms the successful launch and operation of this cutover instance before officially finalizing the migration and archiving the source server.

## AWS Application Migration Service Best Practices

Here are some of the measures recommended by AWS, which you can take to ensure a successful migration with MGN.

### Planning

Build a comprehensive plan before initiating the installation of the AWS Replication Agent on your source servers. This lays the groundwork for a smooth migration process, ensuring that all necessary prerequisites and dependencies are addressed. It involves assessing the compatibility of your applications with AWS, estimating the required downtime (if any), and identifying potential challenges that may arise during the migration.

It’s advised not to reboot your source servers or alter their configurations before completing a cutover to AWS. These actions can introduce variables that might complicate the replication process or cause unforeseen issues during migration. Also important is maintaining a clear and uninterrupted connection between your source server and AWS until the cutover instance is fully operational in AWS is vital.

### Testing

Test your applications at least two weeks before the planned migration date. This timeframe allows for thorough testing of the application in the AWS environment, ensuring that any issues can be resolved before the cutover.

During this phase, validate connectivity to your test instances—using SSH for Linux-based applications or RDP for Windows-based applications—and conduct acceptance tests to confirm that your applications function correctly in their new cloud environment.

### Implementation

Deploy the AWS Replication Agent on your source servers. This establishes a connection between your on-premises environment and AWS, enabling the replication of data. During implementation, monitor the data replication status, ensuring it remains in a “Healthy” state. This monitoring process aids in identifying any issues early to avoid delays in the migration timeline.

Next, conduct a test launch of instances approximately one week before the scheduled cutover date. This allows for the identification and resolution of last-minute issues that may impact the migration success, such as misconfigurations or AWS limits that could hinder instance launch.

Finally, on the planned cutover date, launch the cutover instances for your servers. Verify that these instances are operational to confirm a successful migration before decommissioning the source servers.

## AWS Application Migration Service Limitations

Application Migration Service operates within defined service quotas to ensure optimal performance and resource availability. This introduces several limitations:

* **Cap on concurrent jobs in progress:** This is set at 20 for each supported AWS Region. A job encompasses actions like launching test or cutover instances and cleanup activities. This quota means that only a maximum of 20 such tasks can run simultaneously, with completed jobs not counting against this limit. For organizations with extensive migration needs, this could necessitate prioritizing migrations or seeking a quota increase.
* **Maximum number of active source servers:** This is restricted to 150 servers per AWS Region at any given time. For larger migration projects that exceed this number, the organizations must either split the migration process into separate phases or contact AWS Support for a potential increase in quota.
* **Limit on non-archived source servers:** These servers are capped at 4,000 per Region. This includes all servers under management by MGN in a non-archived state, whether they’re actively replicating or queued for replication. It may be necessary to archive or decommission servers post-migration to free up space within this quota.

Please follow these guidelines to create your summary:

1. Identify and preserve the main topic or purpose of the webpage.
2. Retain key facts, statistics, and data points that are central to the content's message.
3. Keep important quotes from credible sources or experts.
4. Maintain the chronological order of events if the content is time-sensitive or historical.
5. Preserve any lists or step-by-step instructions if present.
6. Include relevant dates, names, and locations that are crucial to understanding the content.
7. Summarize lengthy explanations while keeping the core message intact.

When handling different types of content:

- For news articles: Focus on the who, what, when, where, why, and how.
- For scientific content: Preserve methodology, results, and conclusions.
- For opinion pieces: Maintain the main arguments and supporting points.
- For product pages: Keep key features, specifications, and unique selling points.

Your summary should be significantly shorter than the original content but comprehensive enough to stand alone as a source of information. Aim for about 25-30 percent of the original length, unless the content is already concise.

Present your summary in the following format:

```
{
   "summary": "Your summary here, structured with appropriate paragraphs or bullet points as needed",
   "key_excerpts": "First important quote or excerpt, Second important quote or excerpt, Third important quote or excerpt, ...Add more excerpts as needed, up to a maximum of 5"
}
```

This webpage is a Faddom article about the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN), a tool for migrating applications to AWS from on-premises or other cloud environments. It is part of Faddom's series on Application Migration.

**What AWS MGN Does:** AWS Application Migration Service automates moving applications to AWS, supporting physical servers, virtual machines, and other clouds. It replicates servers in real-time with minimal downtime, allowing applications to run during migration with little to no modification needed.

**Use Cases:** (1) Data Center Migration — move workloads like SAP, Oracle, and SQL Server from VMware vSphere or Microsoft Hyper-V to AWS; (2) Disaster Recovery — continuous replication enables quick failover; (3) Test and Development — create isolated test environments from production replicas; (4) Cloud-to-Cloud Migration — migrate from other clouds or across AWS Regions/Availability Zones/accounts; (5) Physical to Cloud Migration — migrate physical servers with minimal application modification.

**Pricing:** Free for 90 days (2,160 hours per source server), starting when the AWS Replication Agent is installed. Beyond the free period, AWS charges $0.042 per hour (~$30 per server per month) for continued replication. Additional charges apply for supporting AWS infrastructure like EC2 and EBS.

**Expert Tips (from Lanir Shacham, CEO of Faddom):** Use Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation/Terraform) after migration; exclude non-critical data and use AWS Data Lifecycle Manager to minimize storage costs; pre-warm test instances before cutover; monitor replication health with CloudWatch; prepare a rollback strategy with full backups before cutover.

**Workflow (7 stages):** Install AWS Replication Agent (or MGN vCenter Client for agentless); perform initial sync; launch test instances and run acceptance tests; delete test instances if successful; wait for cutover window and redirect traffic; stop operational services on source server; launch cutover instance and archive source server.

**Best Practices:** Plan comprehensively before installing agents; don't reboot or alter source servers before cutover; test applications at least two weeks before migration; validate connectivity (SSH for Linux, RDP for Windows); deploy agent and monitor replication status (keep "Healthy"); test-launch instances one week before cutover; verify cutover instances before decommissioning source servers.

**Limitations:** Maximum 20 concurrent jobs per AWS Region; maximum 150 active source servers per Region; cap of 4,000 non-archived source servers per Region.

**Faddom Promotion:** The article promotes Faddom's application dependency mapping tool, which is agentless, requires no credentials, costs from $10K/year, maps environments in real-time (24/7), and lets one person map an entire data center in an hour. Faddom offers a free 14-day trial with no credit card required.

# AWS Transform MGN FAQs

## General

### What is AWS Transform MGN?

[AWS Transform MGN](/application-migration-service/) is the recommended service for migrations to AWS. AWS Transform MGN simplifies and expedites your migration to AWS by automatically converting your source servers from physical, virtual, or cloud infrastructure to run natively on AWS. It further simplifies your migration and reduces costs by allowing you to use the same automated process for a wide range of applications, without changes to applications, their architecture, or the migrated servers. You can use AWS Transform MGN to perform non-disruptive tests prior to cutover. After testing, you can use AWS Transform MGN to quickly migrate your applications to the cloud during a short cutover window, typically measured in minutes. You can also use AWS Transform MGN to automate application modernizations on your migrated servers.

### How do I get started with AWS Transform MGN?

To start using AWS Transform MGN, simply [click here](https://console.aws.amazon.com/mgn/home) or sign into the AWS Management Console and navigate to “AWS Transform MGN” in the “Migration & Transfer” category. You can follow the steps provided in the console to set up and operate AWS Transform MGN or refer to the [Quick Start Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/quick-start-guide-gs.html).

The [AWS Transform MGN – A Technical Introduction](https://www.aws.training/Details/eLearning?id=71732) training is recommended if you want to learn more about how to use the service, or if you are assisting customers with a migration using AWS Transform MGN. This free online training is offered by AWS Training and Certification, and covers key concepts, service architecture, and implementation approaches for AWS Transform MGN.

### What source infrastructure does AWS Transform MGN support?

You can use AWS Transform MGN to migrate your applications to AWS from physical servers, VMware vSphere, Microsoft Hyper-V, and other cloud providers. You can also use AWS Transform MGN to migrate Amazon EC2 instances between AWS Regions or between AWS accounts, and to [migrate from EC2-Classic to a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/vpc-migrate.html).

### What operating systems and applications are supported by AWS Transform MGN?

AWS Transform MGN allows you to migrate physical, virtual, and cloud source servers to AWS for a variety of [supported operating systems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/Supported-Operating-Systems.html) (OS). AWS Transform MGN supports commonly used applications such as SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server.

### How can I receive product support for AWS Transform MGN?

Contact [AWS Premium Support](/premiumsupport/) to receive product support for AWS Transform MGN according to your support plan.

### What does “MGN” stand for?

“MGN” is an abbreviation of the word “migration.”

## AWS Transform MGN and other AWS services

### Which AWS migration service should I choose?

AWS Transform and AWS Transform MGN are the recommended services for migrations to AWS. You can learn about use cases that may require using a different migration service on the [When to Choose AWS Transform MGN](/application-migration-service/when-to-choose-aws-mgn/) page.

## Pricing and billing

### How am I charged for AWS Transform MGN?

For each source server that you want to migrate, you can use AWS Transform MGN for a free period of 2,160 hours, which is 90 days when used continuously.

The free period starts as soon as you install the AWS Replication Agent on your source server and continues during active source server replication.

If you do not complete your migration of a specific server within the free period, you will be charged per hour while you continue replicating that server. Most customers complete migrations of servers within the allotted free period.

Note that while your source servers are actively replicating, including during the free period, you will incur charges for any AWS infrastructure that is provisioned by AWS Transform MGN to facilitate data replication. You will also incur charges for resources that are provisioned when you launch test or cutover instances, such as compute (Amazon EC2) and storage (Amazon EBS) resources, according to your [AWS pricing plan](/pricing/).

Please refer to the [AWS Transform MGN pricing page](/application-migration-service/pricing/) for more details.

## Security and AWS Region availability

### How is my data encrypted while in transit from my source server to AWS using AWS Transform MGN?

Your replicated data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2, and is transferred directly from your source servers to your VPC. Your data is also encrypted at rest on AWS using [Amazon EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/ebs-encryption.html).

### Can I avoid using the public internet to replicate my data to AWS using AWS Transform MGN?

Yes, with AWS Transform MGN you can control the data replication path using private connectivity options such as a VPN, [AWS Direct Connect](/directconnect/), VPC peering, or another private connection. Learn more about [private connectivity options with AWS Transform MGN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/use-private-ip.html).

### How can I learn more about keeping my data secure when using AWS Transform MGN?

Please refer to the [Security in AWS Transform MGN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/security.html) documentation to understand how to apply the [shared responsibility model](/compliance/shared-responsibility-model/) when you use AWS Transform MGN.

### In what AWS Regions is AWS Transform MGN available?

Please refer to the [AWS Regional Services List](/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regional-product-services/) for the most up-to-date information.

AWS Migration Hub is no longer open to new customers as of November 7, 2025. For capabilities similar to AWS Migration Hub, explore [AWS Transform](https://aws.amazon.com/transform).

# What is AWS Migration Hub Orchestrator?

AWS Migration Hub Orchestrator simplifies and automates the migration of servers and enterprise
applications to AWS. You can get started quickly through the predefined workflow templates
which are built leveraging the migration experience of AWS which also adhere to best
practices. You can also use Migration Hub Orchestrator to automate the error-prone manual tasks involved in the
migration process and orchestrate the related migration tools from start to finish in the Migration Hub Orchestrator
console.

Migration Hub Orchestrator offers templates to create a migration workflow that can be customized to fit your
unique migration requirements. Migration Hub Orchestrator automates the steps in your chosen workflow and
displays the status of migration.

Migration Hub Orchestrator currently supports the following use cases for migration:

Importing virtual machine (VM) images

Migrating SAP NetWeaver applications and HANA databases

Rehosting applications on Amazon EC2

Rehosting SQL Server databases to Amazon EC2 using SQL Server's native backup and
restore

Replatforming SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS

Replatforming applications to Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate.

You can use a predefined workflow template to orchestrate the validation of the source
environment for migration readiness, provision your target environment, migrate databases and
applications, perform post-migration validation, and cutover to AWS.

You can access Migration Hub Orchestrator from [https://console.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/orchestrator/]( https://console.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/orchestrator/) or from the AWS Command Line Interface. For
more information about the Migration Hub Orchestrator APIs and how to use the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), see the [AWS Migration Hub Orchestrator API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub-orchestrator/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html) and the [AWS Migration Hub Orchestrator CLI Command
Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/migrationhuborchestrator/).

## Are you a first-time user of Migration Hub Orchestrator?

If you are a first-time user of Migration Hub, we recommend that you begin by reading the following sections:

**Setting up** – The [Setting up to use Migration Hub Orchestrator](./setting-up.html) section details what you need to set up before using
Migration Hub Orchestrator.

**Templates** – The [Migration Hub Orchestrator templates](./templates.html) section details the templates offered by
Migration Hub Orchestrator for different migration use cases.

**Workflows** – The [Migration workflows for Migration Hub Orchestrator](./migration-workflows.html) section details how
workflows function in Migration Hub Orchestrator.

## Related services

If you are new to Migration Hub, you can refer to the following guides.

[Application Discovery Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/what-is-appdiscovery.html)

[AWS App2Container](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/app2container/latest/UserGuide/what-is-a2c.html)

[AWS Application Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/what-is-application-migration-service.html)

[AWS Launch Wizard for SAP](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/launchwizard/latest/userguide/what-is-launch-wizard-sap.html)

[AWS Launch Wizard for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/launchwizard/latest/userguide/what-is-launch-wizard.html)

[VM Import/Export](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vm-import/latest/userguide/what-is-vmimport.html)

## Pricing

Migration Hub Orchestrator is available to you at no additional cost. You only pay for the AWS resources that
you provision for migrations. For more information, see [AWS Migration Hub pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing).

This page is the official AWS documentation for "What is AWS Migration Hub Orchestrator?" It describes the service as a tool that simplifies and automates the migration of servers and enterprise applications to AWS. It offers predefined workflow templates built from AWS migration experience and best practices, enabling users to automate error-prone manual tasks and orchestrate migration tools from start to finish in the console. Key capabilities include customizing migration workflows and displaying migration status.

The service supports several migration use cases: importing virtual machine (VM) images, migrating SAP NetWeaver applications and HANA databases, rehosting applications on Amazon EC2, rehosting SQL Server databases to Amazon EC2 using native backup and restore, replatforming SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS, and replatforming applications to Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate. Users can access it via the console at https://console.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/orchestrator/ or through the AWS CLI.

Important note: AWS Migration Hub is no longer open to new customers as of November 7, 2025. For similar capabilities, AWS points users to AWS Transform. Migration Hub Orchestrator is offered at no additional cost—users only pay for the AWS resources they provision for migrations.

For first-time users, the documentation recommends reading sections on Setting up, Templates, and Workflows. Related AWS services include Application Discovery Service, AWS App2Container, AWS Application Migration Service, AWS Launch Wizard for SAP, AWS Launch Wizard for SQL Server, and VM Import/Export.

# AWS Migration Hub Pricing - Cost & Features Guide

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/BwxztZWkAtzM2PDRD0cvlf056Po.png?width=1204&height=1612)

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/Oc6QFYEo46OcK9wukvsHlN4Occ.svg?width=376&height=209)

Ready to start optimizing on your cloud spend?

By submitting your email, you agree to opt in to marketing emails.

Migrating to the cloud is revolutionary for companies. It’s not only about shifting workloads but also about optimizing infrastructure, scaling, and remaining competitive in this fast-evolving digital world. [**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/?nc=sn&loc=0) simplifies this with a single tool that you can use for managing, monitoring, and even migrating your projects. But how much will it cost? For professionals planning a move to the cloud, knowing [**AWS Migration Hub pricing**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3) and the relevant costs drivers is very important.

With the proliferation of businesses adopting cloud solutions, we can expect cloud migration to **grow by 25%**. This blog attempts to explain AWS Migration Hub’s features, and pricing and offers tips on how one can minimize expenses while migrating to the cloud.

## **What is AWS Migration Hub?**

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/JlcGZ5bKZ5DMT0KtugP8hrE5dQ.png?width=1600&height=755)

**(Image Source:** [**AWS Migration**](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/deep-dive-on-an-aws-migration-hub-refactor-spaces-environment/)**)**

[**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/?nc=sn&loc=0) is a service within [**Amazon Web Services**](https://aws.amazon.com/) aimed at facilitating easier migration of applications, data and infrastructure to the cloud. It helps manage the entire migration process by providing a single place from which businesses can monitor all migration efforts through an intuitive dashboard.

### **Key Features:**

* **Monitor Migration from a Single Interface:** Track the migration statuses of applications, databases, and servers over a diverse set of AWS and other vendor applications in one interface.
* **Journey Templates:** Predefined workflows and templates for common migration scenarios.
* **Application and Server Discovery:** Tools such as AWS Discovery Agent and Application Discovery Service can be employed to analyze and map the current infrastructure and dependencies.
* **AWS Service Integration:** The Migration Hub is integrated with other AWS infrastructure services such as AWS Database Migration Service and AWS Server Migration Service for easier migration.

[**AWS Migration Hub offers**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/features/?nc=sn&loc=2) much more than just tracking. It helps teams focus on better collaboration, lower the risk of long downtimes, and enhance cost visibility which helps the migration process occur much smoother.

## **How Does AWS Migration Hub Work?**

1. **Assess Your Environment**: Use [**AWS Application Discovery Service**](https://aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/) to gather data on your existing on-premises environment, such as servers, applications, and dependencies.
2. **Plan Your Migration Path**: Group resources into applications and define the migration strategy for each (e.g., rehost, re-platform, or refactor).
3. **Monitor Migration Progress**: Track the progress and performance of your migrations from a single dashboard, providing transparency and accountability across teams.
4. **Leverage Cost Management Tools**: Tools like [**AWS Cost Explorer**](https://pump.co/blog/how-to-use-aws-cost-explorer-to-understand-aws-costs) and tags automatically track migration costs, enabling businesses to compare on-premises expenses versus cloud-based savings.

### **Benefits During Migration:**

* Clear visibility into migration status.
* Reduced risk of unplanned service disruption.
* Increased efficiency with the use of process templates and automation.

## **Deep Dive into AWS Migration Hub Pricing Structure**

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/WS0xFgyBvqFKfRb9SLOkxCMPSqs.png?width=1600&height=781)

Most users assume some components of the [**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3) should have separate charges. In reality, using the Migration Hub for collecting discovery data, planning migration, or tracking progress does not incur any costs. Costs occur from the tools and resources used in AWS while migrating the resources.

#### **1. Data Transfer Costs:**

[**You’ll incur charges for transferring data in and out of AWS**](https://pump.co/blog/aws-data-transfer-pricing). This includes costs associated with network usage and any necessary bandwidth adjustments.

#### **2. Storage Costs:**

AWS charges for the storage of migrated data or VM images. For instance:

* [**Amazon Elastic Block Store**](https://pump.co/blog/amazon-ebs-pricing) is billed based on your selected volume type and the amount of data you store.
* [**Amazon S3**](https://pump.co/blog/amazon-s3-pricing) offers scalable storage but comes with tiered pricing models.

#### **3. Additional AWS Services Fees:**

Migration Hub integrates with services like:

* [**AWS Database Migration Service**](https://aws.amazon.com/dms/): Billed by the instance hours and data replication volume.
* [**AWS Application Migration Service**](https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/): Pricing varies based on VM usage, network traffic, and storage requirements.

#### **4. Refactor Spaces:**

Migration Hub Refactor Spaces introduces additional costs like:

* **$0.028 per** [**environment**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3#:~:text=custom%20estimate%20now%C2%A0%C2%BB-,Environments,-You%20can%20use) **per hour** after the free trial period.
* **$0.000002 per** [**API request**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3#:~:text=in%20Refactor%20Spaces.-,API%20requests,-Refactor%20Spaces%20service), with 500,000 free API requests per month.

### **Comparison with On-Premises Migration Costs:**

One of the major disadvantages of an on-premises migration is the expense associated with hardware, IT services, and software licenses that must be bought up front. With the [**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/?nc=sn&loc=1), businesses making the transition to the cloud do not have to incur these expenses and can instead adopt a **pay-as-you-go model**, which is undoubtedly more affordable.

## **Additional Pricing Benefits**

1. **AWS Free Tier**:

* [**Get 2,160 hours of free usage**](https://aws.amazon.com/free/?gclid=Cj0KCQiAwOe8BhCCARIsAGKeD56KZDdfmCCNt1hASRR_GklEXDaQTnlvlUBrpOb9H9v_mn3WRmrdGi0aAjZKEALw_wcB&trk=2738afd4-9401-4d18-8e3e-1b1c194dea07&sc_channel=ps&ef_id=Cj0KCQiAwOe8BhCCARIsAGKeD56KZDdfmCCNt1hASRR_GklEXDaQTnlvlUBrpOb9H9v_mn3WRmrdGi0aAjZKEALw_wcB:G:s&s_kwcid=AL!4422!3!509606977827!p!!g!!aws%20amazon%20com!12618685604!120373367976&all-free-tier.sort-by=item.additionalFields.SortRank&all-free-tier.sort-order=asc&awsf.Free%20Tier%20Types=*all&awsf.Free%20Tier%20Categories=*all) of Refactor Spaces environments every month for three months, which is equivalent to running three environments for three months.
* Receive 500,000 [**API calls at no charge**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3) every month for Refactor Spaces.

1. **Cost Management Tools**:

* [**AWS Cost Explorer**](https://pump.co/blog/how-to-use-aws-cost-explorer-to-understand-aws-costs) and tags such as **aws:migrationhub** companies can track their expenses in real-time and set budgets more efficiently.
* The business compute costs can be reduced using [**Spot Instances and Reserved Instances**](https://pump.co/blog/aws-spot-vs-reserved-instances).

## **Case Study: Affinidi’s Success with AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces**

[**Affinidi**](https://www.affinidi.com/) is a data empowerment technology startup and had issues with managing an extensive range of 20 API endpoints with various security protocols. This did not aid in the company’s development by stifling agility, increasing developer effort, and further disintegrating services.

[**Affinidi took advantage of AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces**](https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/case-studies/affinidi-case-study/?did=cr_card&trk=cr_card) to streamline and enhance their operations substantially. They consolidated the 20 disparate API endpoints into a singular API layer. This reduced developer effort for **service APIs by 50%** while significantly improving stand-up time from days to minutes. Furthermore, an increase in security standards was established alongside a **25% decrease** in monolithic refactoring costs, showcasing the importance of advanced cloud migration tools.

**The Results**:

* Scalable, secure, and flexible architecture achieved.
* Engineers are empowered to focus on innovation and productivity.
* Ability to scale from 100 thousand to **2 million digital vaults by 2025-26**
* Minimized risks and improved performance.

## **Tools and Tips for Cutting AWS Migration Hub Costs**

Here are some actionable ways to optimize your [**AWS Migration Hub costs**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/pricing/?nc=sn&loc=3):

* **AWS Pricing Calculator:** An advanced AWS pricing tool for you looking to move your existing infrastructure to AWS. It is an excellent way to [**determine your budget and possible expenses**](https://calculator.aws/#/) at your organization.
* **AWS Cost Anomaly Detection:** This [**service monitors cloud spending patterns**](https://aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/aws-cost-anomaly-detection/) and applies machine learning algorithms to notify you if costs unexpectedly spike.
* **AWS Budgets:** A feature that enables you to keep tabs on [**their expenses by creating limits**](https://pump.co/blog/aws-budgets) on their spending.

### **Cost Optimization Tips:**

1. **Right Sizing Instances:** The [**right sizing of compute resources**](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/right-sizing.html) for your applications ensures that you are not over provisioning instances. This also helps lower costs while still optimizing performance. While underprovisioning can have a detrimental impact on performance, overprovisioning leads to unnecessary costs.
2. **Plan Migrations During Off-Peak Hours**:Migrations should be scheduled during times when the application is least used to minimize the impact on business operations. Off-peak migrations carry a lesser risk of downtime affecting customers or vital processes.
3. **Remove and Clean Up Unused Resources:** Periodically checking and removing unused virtual machines, storage, or IP addresses can prevent wasted costs and clustered resources. Unused resources result in expenses while decreasing overall efficiency.
4. **Automate Such Tasks:** Using the [**Migration Hub Orchestrator**](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub-orchestrator/latest/userguide/what-is-migrationhub-orchestrator.html) to automate menial tasks greatly saves manual effort and time while minimizing errors. Eliminating human error is one of the main advantages of automation which also ensures that migrations are correctly performed avoiding cost overruns.
5. **Gradual Refactoring**: [**Migration Hub Refactor Spaces**](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub-refactor-spaces/latest/userguide/what-is-mhub-refactor-spaces.html) allows you to incrementally update applications instead of modernizing an entire system at once. This approach reduces risks, lowers costs, and provides for effective system testing without significantly disrupting normal operations.

## **Conclusion**

[**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/?nc=sn&loc=1) facilitates migrating to the cloud, its pricing structure and cost components should be understood for optimal ROI. Cost management during migration can be greatly aided by tools like [**AWS Cost Explorer**](https://aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/aws-cost-explorer/) and optimization techniques.

[**AWS Migration Hub**](https://aws.amazon.com/migration-hub/features/?nc=sn&loc=2) isn't just for tracking purposes; it is an enabler of cost-effective, efficient, and seamless migrations. Whether organizations are modernizing applications, moving workloads, or adopting a cloud-first strategy, there is always a tool from AWS Migration Hub to assist.

**Get started with AWS Migration Hub and embrace the future of cloud technology.**

This is a Pump.co blog article titled "AWS Migration Hub Pricing - Cost & Features Guide" (8 min read) that provides a comprehensive guide to AWS Migration Hub's pricing structure, features, and cost optimization strategies.

**What is AWS Migration Hub:** AWS Migration Hub is a service within Amazon Web Services that helps businesses manage, monitor, and migrate applications, data, and infrastructure to the cloud. Key features include: monitoring migration from a single interface, journey templates with predefined workflows, application and server discovery tools (AWS Discovery Agent and Application Discovery Service), and integration with other AWS services like AWS Database Migration Service and AWS Server Migration Service.

**How It Works (4 steps):** 1) Assess environment using AWS Application Discovery Service, 2) Plan migration path by grouping resources into applications and defining strategy (rehost, re-platform, refactor), 3) Monitor migration progress from a single dashboard, 4) Leverage cost management tools like AWS Cost Explorer and tags.

**Pricing Structure:** Using the Migration Hub itself for collecting discovery data, planning migration, or tracking progress incurs no costs. Costs arise from:
- Data transfer costs (network usage and bandwidth)
- Storage costs (Amazon EBS billed by volume type/data stored; Amazon S3 tiered pricing)
- Additional AWS services fees (AWS DMS billed by instance hours and data replication volume; AWS Application Migration Service varies by VM usage, network traffic, storage)
- Refactor Spaces: $0.028 per environment per hour after free trial; $0.000002 per API request with 500,000 free API requests per month

**Free Tier Benefits:** 2,160 free hours of Refactor Spaces environments monthly for three months (equivalent to three environments for three months), plus 500,000 free API calls per month.

**Case Study - Affinidi:** A data empowerment startup that used AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces to consolidate 20 disparate API endpoints into a single API layer. Results included: 50% reduction in developer effort for service APIs, improved stand-up time from days to minutes, 25% decrease in monolithic refactoring costs, and ability to scale from 100 thousand to 2 million digital vaults by 2025-26.

**Cost Optimization Tips:** Use AWS Pricing Calculator, AWS Cost Anomaly Detection (ML-based), and AWS Budgets. Specific tips include: right-sizing instances, planning migrations during off-peak hours, removing/cleaning up unused resources, automating tasks with Migration Hub Orchestrator, and gradual refactoring with Refactor Spaces.

**Comparison with On-Premises:** Unlike on-premises migration (which requires upfront hardware, IT services, and software license costs), AWS Migration Hub enables a pay-as-you-go model which is more affordable.

The article concludes by promoting Pump.co, which claims to help early-stage startups save up to 60% in cloud costs (free service for AWS and GCP spending optimization). Related blog posts are linked on AWS data transfer pricing, availability zones, Bedrock pricing, and AWS Budgets.

<webpage_content>
##### Insights Blog

# Lift-and-Shift to Azure: A Strategic Cloud Migration Approach

Migrating to the cloud is a cornerstone of digital transformation. Companies of all sizes are turning to cloud solutions to modernize their IT infrastructure, cut costs, and accelerate innovation. One of the most efficient ways to start this journey is through a lift-and-shift migration strategy, also known as rehosting. This method enables businesses to move their existing systems to the cloud quickly and effectively.

At VIAcode, we specialize in a range of migration strategies, including rehosting, refactoring, re-platforming, and rebuilding. Our expertise is recognized through Microsoft specializations in both “Infrastructure & Database Migration” and “Migrating Enterprise Applications to Microsoft Azure.” While we excel in all approaches, this post focuses on the lift-and-shift strategy. Whether you’re moving mission-critical SQL Server applications, SSIS packages, or other complex workloads, our experts ensure that your migration to Azure is non-disruptive, secure, and optimized for peak performance.

Lift-and-shift offers fast, cost-effective migration with minimal changes to your applications, making it ideal for businesses looking to quickly capitalize on the benefits of Azure. Additionally, we offer a [free migration service](https://viacode.com/free-migration/) where our team will evaluate your environment, determine the best strategy, and even execute that strategy at no cost to you.

## What Is the Lift-and-Shift Cloud Migration Strategy?

The lift-and-shift migration strategy is a simple and direct way to migrate to the cloud. This method involves transferring applications and their data from an on-premises environment to the public cloud—in this case, Microsoft Azure—without requiring changes to the code or architecture.

 For businesses needing a fast cloud migration—perhaps due to expiring on-premises infrastructure leases or rising costs—lift-and-shift offers the quickest solution. It’s particularly beneficial for companies using legacy applications such as SQL Server or managing data workflows through SSIS packages. These systems often require extensive reconfiguration or redevelopment to be fully cloud-native, so lift-and-shift allows businesses to quickly move to Azure without the need for complex modifications. By moving these workloads directly to Azure, you can minimize disruption while taking advantage of the cloud’s scalability and security.

## Why Choose Lift-and-Shift to Azure?

 Even though lift-and-shift is a straightforward approach, it unlocks significant benefits once your systems are running in Azure cloud environments. By choosing Microsoft Azure as your public cloud provider, you gain immediate access to a scalable infrastructure, robust security features, and enhanced performance—without the need to rebuild your applications from scratch. This approach is particularly ideal for migrating legacy systems, such as SQL Server applications or SSIS packages, which can be moved with minimal effort while retaining full functionality. These workloads often don’t require the deep reconfiguration that cloud-native architectures demand, making lift-and-shift a practical and efficient solution.

## Key Benefits of Lift-and-Shift Migration

### Minimal Changes to Code or Architecture

The lift-and-shift strategy allows you to migrate to the cloud without requiring significant re-architecting or rewriting of code, whether you’re working with SQL Server, SSIS packages, or other applications. By avoiding these complex modifications, your internal teams can save valuable time and focus on higher-priority projects, reducing the need for additional development resources. This also leads to faster migrations and cost savings, making it an efficient choice for businesses aiming to quickly move their on-premises infrastructure to the public cloud.

### Rapid Migration Process

 For companies facing imminent data center closures or other time-sensitive business needs, lift-and-shift provides a fast track to the Azure cloud. This approach not only enables a rapid transition but also allows businesses to quickly leverage Azure’s scalable infrastructure, robust security, and innovation capabilities. By migrating swiftly, companies can position themselves to scale, innovate, and adapt to changing market demands without delay.

### Scalable and Flexible Resources

Once your applications are in Azure, scaling resources to meet business demands is as easy as flipping a switch. Azure’s flexible pricing models, such as the pay-as-you-go approach, ensure that you only pay for what you use, making it cost-effective for businesses with fluctuating resource needs. To further enhance cost-effectiveness, consider leveraging VIAcode’s [Azure Optimization Assessment](https://viacode.com/services/azure-optimization-assessment/), which typically identifies opportunities to reduce annual Azure costs by up to 30%.

## Why Azure for Lift-and-Shift?

Businesses are increasingly opting for Microsoft Azure as their preferred public cloud provider for a number of reasons. Azure offers a rich suite of tools, seamless integration with hybrid cloud environments, and built-in compatibility with other Microsoft services like Microsoft 365 and Power BI. By using the lift-and-shift migration strategy, companies can quickly move their SQL Server workloads and SSIS packages to Azure, allowing them to start enjoying these benefits immediately.

### Immediate Cost Savings

Migrating to the cloud can yield significant cost reductions. By moving to Azure, companies can eliminate the overhead associated with maintaining physical hardware on-premises. With features like Azure Hybrid Benefit and reserved instances, you can further optimize costs post-migration. Additionally, third-party solutions such as VIAcode’s [Azure Optimization Assessment](https://viacode.com/services/azure-optimization-assessment/) can help identify ongoing opportunities to reduce Azure costs, ensuring that your cloud environment remains efficient and cost-effective.

### Enhanced Security and Compliance

Azure’s robust security features, including Azure Security Center and built-in compliance with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA, provide businesses with the security assurance they need when moving sensitive data to the cloud. For organizations managing SQL databases or complex SSIS packages, this security upgrade is invaluable.

### Faster Time-to-Cloud

The lift-and-shift migration strategy allows businesses to move to the Azure cloud much faster than more complex migration methods, such as re-architecting or re-platforming. In scenarios where companies need to vacate their on-premises infrastructure quickly, lift-and-shift provides the necessary speed to meet tight deadlines.

### **Pathway to Cloud-Native Services**

While lift-and-shift focuses on migrating existing workloads without changes, it also opens the door to further modernization. Once in Azure, businesses can begin taking advantage of cloud-native services like Azure SQL Database or Azure App Service to enhance their applications over time.

## Embracing Cloud-Native Services for Continuous Modernization

This transition to cloud-native services represents a critical next step in the modernization journey. Azure’s robust suite of cloud-native tools offers more than just operational efficiency; it provides a pathway to continuous innovation. By gradually incorporating services such as Azure SQL Database and Azure App Service, businesses can optimize application performance, improve scalability, and lower operational costs. This approach ensures that companies are not just migrating to the cloud but evolving with it, allowing them to stay competitive, agile, and better equipped to meet future demands.

### The Lift-and-Shift Migration Process: Step-by-Step

Successful migrations to Microsoft Azure require detailed planning and execution. Here’s a brief overview of the key steps involved in a lift-and-shift migration:

**1. Pre-Migration Assessment**

Before moving any workloads, it’s essential to evaluate your current on-premises infrastructure. VIAcode offers a [free Azure assessment](https://www.viacode.com/services/azure-optimization-assessment/), helping businesses identify key dependencies, estimate costs, and develop a tailored migration strategy. This is particularly important when moving complex workloads like SQL Server databases or SSIS packages to Azure.

**2. Migration Planning**

Once the assessment is complete, a detailed migration plan is developed. This plan outlines the timeline, key milestones, and the workloads that will be moved, ensuring a smooth and well-coordinated process.

**3. Executing the Migration**

Using tools like [Azure Migrate](https://www.viacode.com/services/azure-migration-services/) and Azure Site Recovery, the migration begins. Critical workloads are migrated with minimal downtime, and data backups are performed to ensure that no data is lost in the process.

**4. Post-Migration Optimization**

Once your systems are in Azure, post-migration optimization ensures that everything runs smoothly. VIAcode provides ongoing Azure Management services, including performance monitoring, cost optimization, and security assessments, to keep your cloud environment efficient and secure over time.

## Overcoming Common Challenges in Lift-and-Shift Migration

While lift-and-shift is a relatively simple approach, there are still challenges that businesses might face during the migration process. VIAcode helps address these issues:

* **Lack of Cloud Expertise**: Not all companies have the internal resources to handle cloud migrations. Partnering with a trusted Azure expert like VIAcode ensures a smooth transition and mitigates the risks of common pitfalls.

* **Post-Migration Performance Optimization:** Simply moving workloads to the cloud doesn’t guarantee optimal performance. VIAcode’s post-migration services help fine-tune your Azure cloud setup to ensure you get the most out of your SQL Server or SSIS packages.

* **Handling Large Data Migrations:** Migrating large datasets can be challenging, but tools like Azure Data Box and Azure Data Migration Service help move data securely and efficiently.

## Start Your Cloud Journey with VIAcode

A lift-and-shift migration to Azure is a cost-effective, secure, and scalable solution for businesses ready to embrace the cloud. Whether you’re moving SQL Server applications, SSIS packages, or other workloads, VIAcode is here to guide you every step of the way—from pre-migration assessments to post-migration optimization. Start your cloud journey today, and experience the benefits of Microsoft Azure for yourself.

# **The 7 Rs of Cloud Migration Explained: Which Strategy Is Right for You?**

![CloudifyOps](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fill:64:64/1*Nz_LYWB-XqyBsHRP9baiYw.png)
